newsitem.title: USA: Coffee, copper prices edge higher, oil falls.
newsitem.headline: Coffee, copper prices edge higher, oil falls.

text.p: Coffee prices rose Tuesday to extend a two-month rally but amid profit-taking by speculators that has cooled off the market.
Heating oil prices fell on expectations that a weekly inventory report would show a year-on-year rise in stocks. Copper rose on a smaller-than-expected increase in stockpiles.

At New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, March coffee closed up 1.80 cents a pound at 147.45 cents after setting a new life-of-contract high at 150.50 cents early in the day. That price was up 44 percent from Dec. 4.
"The technicals are bullish, the fundamentals are bullish," said Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka. "It will probably trend higher as long as nothing changes."
The low levels of coffee stocks in warehouses that are certified for delivery against futures underscored the tight supply situation that has fed the rally.
"The stocks continue to decline," Spilka said.
Concerns that Brazil's upcoming coffee crop would come in far smaller than this season's estimated 27 million bags also have helped fuel the market's recent upswing.

In a report released Monday, British trading house E.D.& F. Man said it expected the Brazilian crop to come in "significantly below" last year's production but ruled out an extremely low crop. It did not give an estimate but said that the impact of new plantings and reasonable weather made it unlikely for Brazil's output to fall below 20 million bags.
Traders also were keeping an eye on news from No. 2 producer Colombia, where independent coffee growers were mulling a possible protest strike against the government.
Colombian coffee shipments have already been delayed by strike of port and transport workers that ended last week.

Copper prices rose due to a smaller-than-expected increase in stockpiles stored in warehouses certified by the London Metal Exchange, the market bellwether. At the New York Mercantile Exchange's Comex division, March copper ended up 1.55 cents at 104.00 cents a pound.
In weekly data, LME copper stocks rose 8,750 metric tons to 200,500 tons.

"The steady rise in LME stocks recently looks to have helped ease the tightness in the prompt market, with cash prices falling sharply today, and spreads narrowing," Refco's New York analyst James Steel said. "But Tuesday's rise in LME stocks was smaller-than-expected, prompting some further shortcovering in forward dates after last week's plunge."

Copper prices have recovered steadily the past three months from the two-year lows hit in mid-1996 when, after the Sumitomo copper trading scandal, prices fell to levels that restricted the supply of scrap onto the prompt market.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange, heating oil prices fell on expectations that weekly oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute would show a year-on-year rise in stocks of distillates, which include heating oil and diesel, for the first time in more than a year.
Heating oil for March delivery settled 1.10 cents a gallon lower at 64.18 cents.

Traders said they expected the API to report a distillate stock decline of between 2 million and 3 million barrels for the week ended Jan. 31. The API reported a weekly fall of 4.12 million barrels, but the total of 115.529 million barrels was above the year-ago level of 115.207 million barrels.

Two cold winters in 1995 and 1996 had cut distillate stocks back so much that the year-on-year shortfall reached 20 million barrels last August and sent heating oil prices to post-Gulf War highs by October. Since then, high distillate output has replenished stocks, as confirmed by Tuesday's data.
March crude oil ended 13 cents lower at $24.02 a barrel, and March gasoline 0.04 cent lower at 68.31 cents a gallon.
At the Chicago Board of Trade, March wheat set a new contract low of $3.56-1/2 a bushel in early trading and closed 3-3/4 cents lower at $3.57-3/4.
Scepticism about a significant pickup in U.S. wheat exports despite a spate of small sales to Taiwan and South Korea Tuesday weighed on sentiment, traders said.
